_comment: The core-declared file form for chimera's project wizard. A PlayStation project is its discs, in the order the game asks for them - or a program to run in place of one - and, if it starts from somebody's progress, the memory cards. The BIOS is not here: it is firmware, which the frontend resolves once and remembers, rather than something a project carries. An arcade board's project is a MAME rom set instead, and what the board keeps in its own non-volatile memory: the machine setting decides which slots are shown.

slots.title: Discs or program
slots.help: What the console runs. Usually a CD image: a .cue with the .bin files it names beside it, a .chd, a single .bin, .img or .iso of one data track, a PlayStation Store .pbp, or an .ecm. A game of several discs lists them all, in order: the first is in the drive at power-on, and the Next Disc, Previous Disc and Disc Swap controls change it when the game asks. It can also be one PlayStation EXECUTABLE (.exe, .psexe, .ps-exe), which is what homebrew and test programs ship as: the tray stays empty and the console is handed the program once its own ROM has started. With nothing here the console boots to its own menu.

slots.title: Memory cards
slots.help: Memory cards the console starts with, for a project that begins from somebody's saved game. A card is a raw 131072-byte image named for its slot: memcard1.mcd for slot 1, memcard2.mcd for slot 2 (a .mcr or .mc from another emulator is the same file under another name - rename it). Emulator > Export Save Data writes the cards back out under the same names. A card under any other name is refused, rather than ignored.

slots.title: Rom set
slots.help: The game's MAME rom set: the .zip, named exactly as MAME names it (tekken.zip, cryptklr.zip), because the name is how the set is recognised - a renamed zip is an unknown game. It must be a complete (non-merged) set of a current MAME release: every rom the game needs under the name MAME gives it now, a clone's shared roms included. A game with a hard disk or a CD has it as a .chd, named as MAME names it (420uaa04.chd); put it here beside the zip. The board's own firmware, where it is a separate archive, comes from the firmware list and not from here.

slots.title: Board memory
slots.help: What the board keeps with the power off: the EEPROM with the operator's settings and the high scores, a flash card. Optional - without it the board starts blank, as a new one did, and may spend its first boot initialising it. The files are the ones Export Save Data writes, and are read by their names (at28c16.nv, eeprom.nv): the board says which it keeps, and a file under another name is refused.
